transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Time: 16:00 UTC (45 minutes)
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Maya Rodriguez (SummitWorks Legal), Tom Halvorsen (SummitWorks Procurement), Priya Singh (SummitWorks Head of Platform), Evan Cole (SummitWorks Security)

Summary:
Quick procurement / legal check-in to align on outstanding MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs, pricing approvals and next steps for vendor onboarding. Action items captured; agreed to exchange documents and schedule technical benchmark next week.

Topics:
- MSA redlines (indemnity, liability cap, IP, termination)
- DPA clauses (data residency, deletion, subprocessors, KMS)
- SLA targets (uptime, latency, remedies)
- Pricing approvals and purchase order process
- Security artifacts (SOC 2, pen test, encryption)

Action items (recorded above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to run through the redlines you sent and make sure we're aligned on the path to signature and onboarding. I'm on the line with Jordan from our SE team.
[00:08] Jordan Lee: Hi folks. I'll focus on the technical and security asks, yeah, and follow up with the docs.
[00:12] Maya Rodriguez: Thanks. We have a few legal concerns in the MSA and some DPA items we need clarified before procurement can push to PO.
[00:20] Tom Halvorsen: Right, procurement needs the pricing approval and the final MSA sign-off to get the PO through our systems. Timeline's a bit tight, so we wanted to see what's realistic.
[00:28] Priya Singh: From platform, we need guarantees around data residency and the ability to run in our VPC. Also SLA for latency for real-time inference, and a clear roadmap for Dedicated/private deployment.
[00:38] Samir Patel: Totally — makes sense. On the MSA, high level: the liability cap and indemnity language you redlined, we can discuss what are must-haves vs negotiables. Our standard is typically a cap tied to fees paid over 12 months.
[00:48] Maya Rodriguez: The legal team prefers a 24-month lookback and higher caps for IP infringement. Also we're pushing for mutual indemnity on third-party claims related to model outputs.
[00:58] Jordan Lee: (background) Sorry, just to add on the model outputs, we have controls around content filtering and we can enable usage-level guardrails, but we usually recommend including explicit disclaimers in the product.
[01:05] Evan Cole: For security, we need to confirm KMS options — customer-managed keys for data at rest? We saw note in the DPA but need specifics: is bring-your-own-key (BYOK) supported in private deployments?
[01:15] Jordan Lee: Yes, in our Private and Dedicated offerings customers can integrate with their KMS, HSM. In hosted there's an option to use customer KMS for encrypting customer data at rest — we'll send the integration notes.
[01:24] Maya Rodriguez: Also subprocessors list — your DPA references them but it's quite broad. Can we get current subprocessor inventory and a commitment to notify before new ones are added?
[01:33] Samir Patel: Absolutely. Jordan will share the current subprocessor list and we can include notification language; we typically do 30 days notice for material changes.
[01:40] Tom Halvorsen: On SLAs — uptime is one thing, but Priya is particularly concerned about token latency for inference. What are typical p95/p99s for the Dedicated environment?
[01:49] Jordan Lee: In Dedicated we see p95 generation latency under 200ms for short prompts on recent quantized models; p99 can vary by model and sequence length. We can run a benchmark on your expected prompts and provide a report.
[01:58] Priya Singh: That benchmark would be helpful; our use-case is sub-300ms interactive responses for a customer-facing assistant. If p99 exceeds that we need auto-fallback to a smaller model to preserve latency SLA.
[02:08] Jordan Lee: We have routing and fallback policies that can do that — automatic model fallback is supported, and cache/prefix caching will also help. We'll propose a config as part of the technical bench.
[02:18] Maya Rodriguez: Back to the MSA redlines: termination for convenience — you're proposing 30 days notice, we want to ensure data return and deletion obligations extend beyond termination with certification.
[02:27] Samir Patel: We can add a data return and secure deletion clause with a 90-day retention window post-termination and provide a certification of deletion. For hosted environments, we'll need to confirm backup retention windows in writing.
[02:36] Evan Cole: And what about audit rights? Our compliance team often asks for right to audit or for a SOC 2 + annual pen test with remediation timelines.
[02:44] Jordan Lee: We can share our SOC 2 Type II report; customers can request vendor assessments and we provide a scope of pen test results summary. Full on-site audits are typically limited but we can offer a questionnaire and remediation timelines.
[02:54] Tom Halvorsen: On pricing approvals — do you have a standard PO template or do we need to go through procurement redline? Also is there any discounting tiers for a committed Dedicated pool?
[03:03] Samir Patel: We have standard PO language and an enterprise sales ops team that will accept your PO. For Dedicated commits, we do tiered discounts based on committed spend and term — Jordan can provide a pricing sheet.
[03:11] Priya Singh: What's the approval lead time from Redwood side once we submit a PO and signed MSA? We have internal milestones dependent on vendor onboarding.
[03:18] Samir Patel: Once MSA signed and PO issued, onboarding can begin within two weeks typically; Dedicated capacity provisioning may add 2-4 additional weeks depending on region and GPU availability.
[03:27] Maya Rodriguez: One more legal ask — indemnity carveouts around model outputs and regulatory fines. We need to understand how Redwood handles claims that arise from model hallucinations affecting customers.
[03:36] Jordan Lee: We don't take on liability for customer product decisions; many customers include use restrictions and disclaimers. We can discuss narrower carveouts, but broad liability for model outputs is a tough ask from our legal/underwriting perspective.
[03:46] Maya Rodriguez: Understood. We'll mark that as a substantive issue and get internal guidance; will likely request a higher cap or carveouts for IP.
[03:53] Tom Halvorsen: For signature, do you require SSO or other onboarding steps to create accounts? Procurement can't sign until we've validated SSO/SCIM provisions and RBAC.
[04:02] Jordan Lee: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; RBAC can be integrated with your IdP. We'll include a checklist for onboarding steps: SSO, IP allowlist, initial API keys, and any VPC peering if private.
[04:11] Samir Patel: Ok, let's recap next steps real quick. Jordan will send security artifacts (SOC2, architecture diagram, subprocessor list), I'll send the redlined MSA/DPA back to Maya with a short change log, and Priya/Tom will check procurement timeline and PO workflow.
[04:22] Priya Singh: Yes, and we'll aim to get pricing approved at our procurement meeting on 2026-07-01. If we need a formal quote for that committee, please send the pricing sheet.
[04:31] Maya Rodriguez: I'll focus on the MSA redlines and flag any non-starters by Tuesday. If we can get a mutual agreement on the indemnity language then procurement can finalize the PO.
[04:39] Samir Patel: Great. Any other questions?
[04:42] Evan Cole: One last: do you have a standard data processing addendum versioning? We want to ensure it maps to EU data residency laws for our EU customers.
[04:50] Jordan Lee: We have regional DPA variants — Jordan will attach the EU-specific DPA and note residency controls.
[04:56] Tom Halvorsen: Perfect. That should cover it. Thanks everyone.
[04:59] Samir Patel: Thanks all — we'll follow up with docs. Expect Jordan's packet and my redlines by EOD Friday.

End of call.
